description: Flat stamped steel mounting bracket/strap. Exactly 3 holes: two plain round smooth-bore holes and ONE serrated splined/toothed-bore hole designed to mate with a matching serrated pin. 'VA' is embossed into the surface between the middle hole and the plain end-hole, on the side of the middle hole opposite the serrated hole.

identity.summary: A flat, thin, elongated steel strap with rounded ends and exactly three in-line holes, one of which has a serrated (cog/scallop-toothed) bore. Often shows a 'VA' emboss on the face.
distinguishing_features: flat thin strap silhouette (length much greater than width), rounded ends
exactly 3 holes arranged in a straight line
ONE of the holes has a serrated/toothed bore (the others are plain round)
usually a 'VA' embossed mark on the face
bright zinc / rainbow-passivated or bare-metal finish
not_to_confuse_with: bearing_cup (a round/cylindrical deep-drawn CUP with a rim and central bore, NOT a flat strap)

serration_missing.signature: The designated serrated hole appears as a smooth round bore instead of a repeating tooth/scallop profile. IDENTIFY THE SERRATED HOLE BY SIZE: it is the LARGEST of the three holes (the two plain holes are visibly smaller); the mark ALWAYS belongs on that biggest hole, never on a small plain hole or on blank metal. Compare it to the part's own smaller plain holes in the same image; if the largest hole looks identical to a plain hole (a smooth round bore, no teeth), serration is missing.
glare_rule: GLARE-ROBUST CHECK (critical for bare-bright/washed-out photos): teeth are decided by the hole's OUTER EDGE OUTLINE, not by the brightness of the bore.

Even when the bore is blown out to solid white by glare, a serrated hole still shows a scalloped/cog-toothed EDGE (a ring of tiny bumps) around its rim, while a plain hole shows a perfectly smooth circular edge.
Judge serration from the rim silhouette.
Only call serration_missing if the rim of the designated hole is clearly a smooth circle with NO scallops.
If glare makes the rim genuinely unreadable, do NOT guess serration_missing - lower confidence / NEEDS_REVIEW instead.
localization: BBOX MUST tightly enclose ONLY the single serrated hole - the LARGEST-diameter hole of the three - its bore plus its rim, and nothing else.
Centre the box ON that biggest hole.
Do NOT box the whole part, do NOT box a smaller plain hole, and do NOT place the box on blank metal beside a hole.
The marker draws a locator circle inside this bbox, so a tight box centred exactly on the largest hole is required for the mark to land on it.

confidence_model.formula: confidence = sum(weight_i * factor_i) / sum(weight_i). Each factor is judged 0..1 BY EYE from the image (never measured by detection code); the formula only COMBINES those judgments into the reported number so the score is explainable and reproducible.

rim_smoothness.meaning: How clearly the designated hole's RIM OUTLINE is a smooth circle with NO scallops/teeth. 1.0 = obviously smooth & toothless (clearly missing); 0.5 = ambiguous; 0.0 = teeth clearly present (not missing).

evidence_readability.meaning: How readable the rim is: crisp, in-focus, flat and unobstructed. LOWER it for glare wash-out, an oblique angle, or a countersink/dome that hides the true rim outline. 1.0 = crisp & flat; 0.0 = rim unreadable.

anchor_certainty.meaning: How certain the boxed hole is the DESIGNATED serrated hole = the LARGEST of the three. 1.0 = clearly the biggest; lower when the three holes look similar in size.

confidence_model.bands: Interpretation of the result: rim crisply smooth + readable + clearly the largest hole -> 0.90-1.0; smooth but softened by glare / countersink dome / size ambiguity -> 0.60-0.75; rim genuinely unreadable -> score < 0.60 and set NEEDS_REVIEW (do not assert the defect). Confidence must track HOW CLEAR the missing-teeth evidence is, NOT how severe the defect is.

confidence_rule: CONFIDENCE = HOW CLEAR the missing-teeth evidence is, NOT how severe the defect is.

Compute it as a weighted average of three factors each judged 0..1 BY EYE: rim_smoothness (weight 0.5) = how clearly the designated hole's RIM OUTLINE is a smooth circle with NO scallops/teeth (1.0 obviously toothless, 0 teeth clearly present); evidence_readability (weight 0.3) = how crisp, flat and unobstructed the rim is - LOWER it for glare wash-out, an oblique angle, or a countersink/dome that hides the rim; anchor_certainty (weight 0.2) = how sure the boxed hole is the LARGEST / designated serrated hole. confidence = 0.5*rim_smoothness + 0.3*evidence_readability + 0.2*anchor_certainty.
Bands: crisp + readable + clearly largest -> 0.90-1.0; smooth but softened by glare/countersink/size ambiguity -> 0.60-0.75; rim unreadable -> below 0.60 and NEEDS_REVIEW.
A crisp, obviously-toothless bore MUST score HIGHER than a domed or glare-softened one, even though both are 'serration missing'.

incomplete_embossing.signature: A stamped/embossed alphanumeric character (in the 'VA' mark) is incompletely formed, shallow, faint, or illegible relative to the other character in the same mark. At least one character is PRESENT but clearly shallower/fainter than the other - the visible 'VA' confirms this is the FRONT face (the 'VA' is stamped on the FRONT face only; a fully blank VA zone is the BACK face, not a defect).
localization: LOCATE BY GEOMETRY: the 'VA' mark sits between the MIDDLE hole and the plain end-hole, on the side of the middle hole OPPOSITE the serrated hole (find the serrated hole first, then look at the middle hole's far side).

BBOX MUST be SMALL and tight on the VA mark zone (the affected character[s]) - well under ~0.15 of the image in each dimension - NOT the whole face, NOT over the middle hole, and NOT surrounding blank metal.
Drawn as a plain bounding box only (no inner character segmentation).

va_present.meaning: the 'VA' characters are visible (this confirms the FRONT face; a blank zone is the back face, not this defect).

shallowness_contrast.meaning: one character is clearly SHALLOWER/fainter/less complete than the other (the actual defect).

not_glare.meaning: ruled out glare merely washing out a character - the shallow stroke's groove/shadow is genuinely weak.

embossing_missing.signature: The required 'VA' embossed mark is absent where it is expected on the FRONT face. FRONT/BACK DISCRIMINATOR (VA-INDEPENDENT - decide the face from the OUTER-EDGE PROFILE, not from the VA): on the FRONT (punch-entry) face the outer edge is CHAMFERED / ROLLED-OVER - a rounded bevel band runs around the whole perimeter and both rounded ends (a bright sloped ring where the flat face curves down to the side wall) and the two plain holes are COUNTERSUNK (dished) (reference 164116); on the BACK (die) face the outer edge is SQUARE and SHARP with NO bevel band and the plain holes punch through FLAT (reference 164359). Flag embossing_missing ONLY when the CHAMFERED/ROLLED-edge FRONT face is confirmed yet the VA zone is blank. If the edge is SQUARE and SHARP (back face), a blank VA zone is NORMAL -> OK, never embossing_missing. Rule out glare/shadow/dirt/crop first; if the edge profile is genuinely unreadable, set NEEDS_REVIEW rather than guessing the face.
localization: LOCATE BY GEOMETRY: the 'VA' mark's designated location is between the MIDDLE hole and the plain end-hole, on the side of the middle hole OPPOSITE the serrated hole.
BBOX MUST be SMALL and tight on that VA zone - well under ~0.15 of the image in each dimension - NOT the whole face and NOT over the middle hole.
Drawn as a plain bounding box only.

rulings: MANDATORY CHECKPOINT LIST (gates OK - emit a `checkpoints` entry for EVERY item below on EVERY bracket image, before deciding the result). `OK` is INVALID unless ALL of these are explicitly CLEARED; run each one actively - do NOT wait for an anomaly to catch your eye, because a quiet defect (a missing mark, a single faint groove) looks like normal metal.
The full list:

(1) face - classify FRONT vs BACK from the outer-edge/countersink profile (PREREQUISITE for embossing); (2) serration_missing - the LARGEST hole shows a scalloped/toothed rim; (3) embossing - face+VA per the MANDATORY EMBOSSING CHECKPOINT; (4) line_mark - SWEEP THE WHOLE FACE for thin continuous grooves, including a single faint hairline that runs hole-to-hole (this is the most-missed defect: a thin continuous groove is a line_mark even when it is faint, and a thin DEFINED continuous groove is NOT specular - specular is a broad grain-free gradient band, a line_mark is a narrow defined trace); (5) dark_mark / dark_spot - near-black blemishes (enumerate each, not the passivation tint); (6) white_mark - a localised dull low-luster patch; (7) global defects - corrosion, dent, edge_chip on the profile/edges.
Each item is CLEARED, DEFECT (then also in `defects`), or NEEDS_REVIEW; any unresolved item makes the overall result NEEDS_REVIEW, never OK.
Under-reporting a checkpoint you did not actively run is the same failure as a silent OK.
MANDATORY EMBOSSING CHECKPOINT (gates OK - run it on EVERY bracket image before deciding the result).
Embossing_missing is an ABSENCE defect: a blank VA zone looks like plain metal and will NOT catch your eye, so you MUST actively run this checkpoint every time.
Step 1 (PREREQUISITE) - classify the FACE from the OUTER-EDGE PROFILE, independently of the VA:

FRONT (punch-entry) = a CHAMFERED / ROLLED-OVER bevel band runs around the whole perimeter and both rounded ends AND the two plain holes are COUNTERSUNK (dished) (reference 164116); BACK (die) = the outer edge is SQUARE and SHARP with no bevel band and the plain holes punch through FLAT (reference 164359); if the edge/countersink profile is genuinely unreadable -> NEEDS_REVIEW (do NOT guess the face).
Step 2 - read the VA zone (between the MIDDLE hole and the plain end-hole, on the side of the middle hole OPPOSITE the serrated hole) as present | shallow | blank.
Step 3 - resolve:

FRONT + blank VA -> embossing_missing (sev 4); FRONT + one character clearly shallower -> incomplete_embossing; FRONT + VA present -> embossing CLEARED; BACK + blank VA -> embossing CLEARED (normal back face).
A bracket may NOT be returned OK until this face+VA checkpoint is explicitly CLEARED, and a blank VA zone may NEVER be defaulted to OK without first CONFIRMING the BACK (square, sharp) edge profile.
Emit this as a `checkpoints` entry (check='embossing', with the face + VA evidence) on every image.
Identify the SERRATED hole first as the fixed anatomical anchor before checking anything else. Locate all other features relative to it, never relative to the image frame.

The part has exactly 3 holes: two plain smooth-bore and one serrated toothed-bore. Only the designated serrated hole is evaluated for tooth presence; a plain hole is supposed to be smooth - never flag a plain hole as serration missing.

If the serrated hole shows a smooth fully round bore identical to the plain holes, flag serration_missing - but confirm via the rim outline (scalloped vs smooth), not the bore brightness, because glare can whiten the bore of a good serrated hole.
FRONT/BACK RULE - decide the FACE from the OUTER-EDGE PROFILE FIRST, independently of the 'VA'.

The strap is stamped/blanked, so its two faces differ at the rounded ends and the whole outer perimeter: on the FRONT (punch-entry) face the outer edge is CHAMFERED / ROLLED-OVER - a rounded bevel band runs continuously around the whole perimeter and both rounded ends, showing as a bright sloped ring where the flat face curves down to the side wall, and the two plain holes are COUNTERSUNK (each sits in a shallow dished/rounded depression) (reference 164116); on the BACK (die) face the outer edge is SQUARE and SHARP - the flat face meets the side wall at a crisp ~90-degree outline with NO bevel band, and the two plain holes punch through FLAT (a small sharp burr ring at most, no countersink dish) (reference 164359).
The 'VA' embossing is on the FRONT face ONLY (between the middle hole and the plain end-hole, on the side of the middle hole opposite the serrated hole).
COMBINE face + VA:

(a) chamfered/rolled edge (FRONT) AND 'VA' present -> OK (or incomplete_embossing if a character is shallow); (b) chamfered/rolled edge (FRONT) AND the VA zone blank -> embossing_missing (the mark is genuinely absent on the front face); (c) square sharp edge (BACK) AND the VA zone blank -> the BACK face is shown and that is NORMAL, mark OK, do NOT flag embossing_missing; (d) if the edge profile is genuinely unreadable, fall back to VA presence and if the face stays unresolved mark NEEDS_REVIEW.

Do NOT decide the face from the blank VA zone alone - a blank zone means back face ONLY when the SQUARE sharp edge profile confirms it; on a chamfered/rolled FRONT face a blank VA zone is embossing_missing.

Flag incomplete_embossing when 'VA' is present but one character is clearly shallower/fainter than the other (rule out glare washing out a character first via a tilt-check for the stroke's groove/shadow).
white_mark = a pale, dull, LOW-luster patch (LESS shiny than the surrounding same-face metal) with the brushed grain still visible through it; it does not shift with viewing angle.

Do NOT confuse with (a) specular glare, which is BRIGHTER/shinier than surroundings and grain-free, or (b) the overall rainbow/dull passivation tint that covers the whole face uniformly (that is the finish).
Only flag a LOCALISED dull patch that contrasts with the rest of the same face.

Dark surface defects have TWO tiers only: dark_spot (a few small DISCRETE darker spots, boxed tight on each spot) and dark_mark (a larger SOLID near-black blotch). Classify by the highest-matching tier; there is no dark_speckling category.

line_mark is long, thin and continuous, often spanning a large fraction of the part and crossing holes without breaking; a short localised mark is a scratch. Keep a line crossing a hole as one continuous box.

Scan the ENTIRE part for EVERY defect type on every image: full outer profile, all three holes, both faces, and the embossing zone. Never stop after the first defect; cross-apply a defect type seen on one sample to all others.
Ignore any finding below 0.60 confidence (do not annotate), but a borderline 0.55-0.60 case may deserve a second look via NEEDS_REVIEW.
A part is OK only if it passes every checkpoint: profile, both plain holes, serration presence, embossing presence/location/quality, plating uniformity, no white marks, no line marks/scratches.
notes: Confusions to avoid: dark_mark vs dark_spot vs OK; incomplete_embossing vs embossing_missing; serration_missing vs by-design splined hole; white_mark vs glare/plating tint.
